title: Openings
note: One opening card per origin: it fires in year 1 and says where you are, who you report to and what you do, so the first year starts with context. Written to the plain-English rule: what is happening, why it matters to you, then the joke.

events.title: Four Months In
events.body: You came back from your overseas degree four months ago and were posted to the {ministry} as an Assistant Director. Your reporting officer is {senior}, {senior.aTitle}. Today {senior} hands you your first real job: a paper for the Minister, due in two weeks, on a scheme whose numbers are bad. A scholar's first paper gets read closely.

choices.text: Write that the scheme isn't working, and show the numbers.
choices.outcome: Your paper says plainly that the scheme isn't working, and shows why. {senior} sends it up unchanged. The Minister's office asks who wrote it: half of them want to meet you, and half want to know why nobody stopped you.

choices.text: Write it the way the Minister's office will want to read it.
choices.outcome: Your paper says the scheme is "gaining traction", which is true of its two good months. It goes up on time and comes back with a tick. {senior} says nothing, and doesn't give you a difficult file again for a year.

choices.text: Ask {senior} what the Minister already thinks, first.
choices.outcome: {senior} tells you what the Minister thinks, and which numbers to lead with. The paper lands well. You've learned how papers get written here, and you're not sure you like it.

did: you wrote, in your first paper, that the scheme wasn't working
you called a failing scheme "gaining traction" in your first paper
you asked what the answer was meant to be before writing your first paper

events.title: Eight Months In
events.body: You've been a Management Executive at the {ministry} for eight months, mostly drafting replies to letters from the public. Your reporting officer is {senior}, {senior.aTitle}. {peer}, who joined the same week as you, already gets sent to meetings you don't. Your first appraisal is in four months.

choices.outcome: {senior} gives you a briefing note for a Deputy Secretary, due Friday. It's harder than anything you've done. It goes in on time, with one mistake that {senior} catches before anyone upstairs sees it.

choices.text: Ask {peer} how to get into those meetings.
choices.outcome: {peer} says you just ask to sit in. So you ask. The meetings are mostly about scheduling other meetings, but people upstairs now know your face.

choices.text: Keep your head down and clear the letters.
choices.outcome: You clear a hundred and forty replies by December, each one checked twice. Nobody upstairs counts them. {senior} does, and starts sending you the letters nobody else wants to answer.

did: you asked for harder work, eight months in
you asked your way into meetings, eight months in
you kept your head down and cleared the letters, eight months in
